com.esignal.jstandard.managers

Interface ContentManager

  • All Superinterfaces:
    ResourceManager
    All Known Subinterfaces:
    ProxyManager

    public interface ContentManager
extends ResourceManager
    Purpose of this class is to provide the Content data.

    ContentManager allows users to request Content data . It is in the form of a traditional asynchronous response. ContentRequestListener is required to be passed as part of the request method. Also, ContentRequest object should be populated with appropriate request information e.g. request query , turnaround and response type.

    Content response is sent to the listener onResponse(). Content response information is wrapped as a String object that can be retrieved using the ContentEvent. Also, all request calls are treated separately, they do not depend on each other, thus if the same listener instance is being used on multiple requests than it's clients responsibility to manage onResponse() per symbol.

    We will run through a simple usage of ContentManager. Let's create a factory first. The getFactory() method will retrieves the default implementation of the Factory. The implementation can be changed by calling other getFactory(...) methods OR overriding property "jstandard.resourcemanagerfactory.name" in jstandard.properties. ResourceManagerFactory factory = ResourceManagerFactory.getFactory();

    Now create a ContentManager using the factory. ContentManager contentManager = factory.createContentManager();

    To start the connection we now need to create instances of ConnectionSettings and ConnectionListener. (Implement MyConnectionListener) ConnectionSettings myConnectionSettings = new ConnectionSettings("myhost", "myusername", "mypassword"); //If proxy settings are required //myConnectionSettings.setProxyInfo("phost", pport, "puser", "ppass"); ConnectionListener myConnectionListener = new MyConnectionListener(); contentManager.connect(myConnectionSettings, myConnectionListener); At the start the connection listener will receive an event of connecting and after successful connection connected event.

    To get the response for the analytics request, let's make a request to the ContentManager with a JSON request. But before that we also need to have an implementation of the ContentRequestListener. Fill the ContentRequest object and pass it to the manager along with the listener: 

     
        ContentRequestListener myContentRequestListener = new MyContentRequestListener();
        String jsonQuery = "......";
        CONTENT_REQUEST_FORMAT format = CONTENT_REQUEST_FORMAT.JSON;
        Long turnAround = generateUniqueTurnAround();
        ContentRequest contentRequest = new DefaultContentRequest(jsonQuery, turnAround, format);
        contentManager.request(contentRequest, myContentRequestListener);
    The listener will be receiving the response for the request query.

    To receive the response data please implement ContentRequestListener' onResponse method. From ContentEvent get the response object which should have the response information. The response object is of type String. 

     
        public void onResponse(ContentEvent contentEvent) {
                if (log.isDebugEnabled()) {
                        log.debug(LoggingUtil.sanitize("Content listener response received with:" + contentEvent.getResponse()));
                }
                System.out.println("Content response: " + contentEvent.getResponse());
                System.out.println("Content response turnAround: " + contentEvent.getTurnAround());
        }

    Disconnect from the manager in the end. contentManager.disconnect();
